name: Japanese · Phrases · Greetings and introductions
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.note: To friends, family and close coworkers, until around late morning.
To anyone you'd speak politely to; at work it's used for your first hello at any hour.
Daytime hello to neighbours, shop owners, acquaintances; rare between close friends.
Hello after dark, to neighbours or people you meet in the evening.
The first thing you say when meeting someone; usually followed by your name.

entries.term: よろしくお願いします。
entries.reading: よろしくおねがいします
entries.back: Nice to meet you. / Looking forward to it.
entries.note: Closes a self-introduction; also said when starting to work or study with someone.
Reply to よろしくお願いします or a thank-you; often followed by よろしくお願いします.
Friendly version among peers, e.g. a new classmate or a friend's friend.
To friends, especially when you haven't seen them for a bit. Not an everyday hello.
Polite, for someone you haven't seen in a while; common in letters and emails.

entries.term: 元気だよ。そっちはどう？
entries.reading: げんきだよそっちはどう
entries.note: Natural reply between friends to 元気？

entries.term: おかげさまで元気です。
entries.reading: おかげさまでげんきです
entries.note: Polite reply to お元気ですか; おかげさまで adds warmth, not literal thanks.
To a friend you haven't seen for weeks or months.
Polite version for seniors, clients, or acquaintances.
Follows 久しぶり with a friend you haven't seen for a while.
Warm, to a friend or family member when you finally meet up.

entries.term: お会いできてよかったです。
entries.reading: おあいできてよかったです
entries.note: Said politely when parting after a first meeting.
The everyday goodbye between friends.
To classmates or coworkers you'll see the next day.

entries.back: Hi. / Thanks for your hard work.
entries.note: Greeting among coworkers in the hallway or when leaving; also opens work messages.

entries.reading: おさきにしつれいします
entries.note: Said when leaving work before others; they reply お疲れさまです.
Polite way to take your leave from a visit, meeting or office.
Before bed or when parting late at night; just おやすみ with family and friends.
Said as you walk in the door at home.
Reply to ただいま from whoever is at home.
Said when leaving home (or the office) and coming back later.

entries.back: See you later! Have a good day.
entries.note: Reply to いってきます from the person staying behind.
Said as you step into someone's home or enter their office.
The host welcoming a guest at the door; friendly, not shop language.

entries.term: どちらのご出身ですか？
entries.reading: どちらのごしゅっしんですか
entries.note: Polite question after introductions; asks hometown or country.

entries.term: 名前、なんて呼べばいい？
entries.reading: なまえなんてよべばいい
entries.note: Friendly question to a new friend about a nickname or first name.

entries.reading: きをつけてかえってね
entries.note: Said to a friend or guest as they leave, especially at night.
